body: `.gitignore` lines 14-15 are `*/__init__.py` and `__init__.py`, and line 17 is `tools`. Consequences, verified with `git ls-files` in session 16: lbm/backends/__init__.py has been untracked since T101 (the Backend protocol is not in the repo), and the whole of tools/ is untracked although CLAUDE.md documents `python -m tools.issues` and calls DOCS/ISSUES.jsonl committed. lbm/__init__.py and validate/__init__.py are tracked only because they predate the rule; flow/__init__.py was force-added in session 16. A fresh clone cannot import lbm.backends and has no issue queue tooling. Fix is to drop the two __init__.py lines and the `tools` line from .gitignore and add the missing files - but it touches lbm/ and repo-wide config, so it wants its own task rather than being folded into a product task (DOCS/PLAN2.md Risks, last row).
title: [repo] .gitignore drops every __init__.py: lbm/backends and tools/ are untracked

body:
`myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m validate.autoconfig --backend warp` prints FAIL. Section 1 (accuracy: Plan.estimated_seconds vs a timed run) predicted 5.61 s against an actual 3.78 s, error 48.3% against the rung's 25% limit. Section 2 is unaffected: all 24 sweep cases pass, worst peak |u| 0.0695, worst Re error 0.0000% - the same digits sessions 17 and 18 printed on numpy.

Pre-existing, not a T107 regression. Rung B had only ever been run on numpy (4.2% error in session 17, 15.0% in session 18), and D-059 calibrated the estimator against the numpy column of the DOCS/STATE2.md performance table. On warp the case is 360x390 = 140k cells, which sits between the table's measured 40k (4155 steps/s) and 1M (757 steps/s) rows, and a GPU at that size is partly launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound - so a log-log interpolation of two bandwidth-bound points over-predicts the time. The predictor is pessimistic (predicted slower than actual), which is the safe direction for a user-facing estimate but still outside the rung's own bar.

Fix would be either a warp-specific calibration point near 100-200k cells in the performance table, or an explicit fixed-overhead term in estimated_seconds for GPU backends. Neither belongs in T107.
dropped_reason: measured while this session's own orphaned processes were still running; superseded by a clean-machine measurement
title: [autoconfig] Plan.estimated_seconds is 48% out on the warp backend, so Rung B fails its accuracy check there

`myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m validate.autoconfig --backend warp` prints FAIL. Section 1 (accuracy: Plan.estimated_seconds vs a timed run): predicted 5.61 s, actual 3.19 s, error 75.7% against the rung's 25% limit. Measured on an idle machine, AMD Ryzen 7 5800H at 3201 of 3201 MHz on mains, RTX 3050 Laptop, driver 592.82 (D-035).

Section 2 is unaffected on either backend: 24/24 sweep cases pass, worst peak |u| 0.0695, worst Re error 0.0000% - the same digits sessions 17 and 18 printed. Rung B on numpy is PASS the same day: predicted 61.05 s, actual 56.46 s, error 8.1%.

Pre-existing, not a T107 regression. Rung B had only ever been run on numpy (4.2% session 17, 15.0% session 18) and D-059 calibrated the estimator against the numpy column of the DOCS/STATE2.md performance table. The case is 360x390 = 140k cells, which sits between that table's measured 40k (4155 steps/s) and 1M (757 steps/s) warp rows; a GPU at that size is partly kernel-launch-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, so a log-log interpolation between two bandwidth-bound points over-predicts. The error is in the safe direction for a user-facing estimate (it promises more time than it takes) but is well outside the rung's own bar.

Matters for T110: M8's gate is a wall clock on warp, so an estimator 1.8x out on that backend is the one T110 will lean on. Fix is a warp calibration point near 100-200k cells in the performance table, or an explicit launch-overhead term in estimated_seconds for GPU backends. Neither belongs in T107.

body:
Measured in session 20 through the new flow.Case front door (T108), numpy backend, idle machine: water, 0.005 m/s, 0.02 m, quality=fast (Re 99.6), 78000 steps = 130 convective times, window the last 50%.

  Cd 1.5955 +- 0.0157, Cl amplitude 0.416, St 0.1841 (peak 44x the next distinct one, 12.0 periods), peak |u| 0.09761, 478 s.

Rung 3's published bands are Cd 1.25-1.45 and St 0.155-0.175 (validate/cylinder.py CD_BAND / ST_BAND), and both numbers sit above them. The physics is not in question -- Rung A, R3 and R4 all still print session 11/15/18's digits -- the DOMAIN is different: flow/autoconfig.py chooses SPAN_D=12 (8.3% blockage) and UPSTREAM_D=3, where validate/cylinder.py uses SPAN_D=24 (4.2%) and UPSTREAM_D=8 deliberately, and its own SPAN_D docstring records the measurement that confinement raises Cd: 15 D of span gave Cd 1.4635, 'just over the top of the acceptance band'. 12 D is tighter still.

Why it matters: M8's gate (DOCS/PLAN2.md) is 'validate.minute prints PASS: a PNG of a disc plus physical numbers reaches St 0.155-0.175 and Cd 1.25-1.45 THROUGH flow.Case'. As the constants stand, the product path cannot reach those bands however long it runs, because the domain is the reason and not the run length.

Not a T108 defect and not fixed here (scope): T108 assembles what the Plan sizes. Owner is T110 / Rung E. The fix is a decision in flow/autoconfig.py -- widen SPAN_D/UPSTREAM_D toward Rung 3's, at a cost in cells and therefore in M8's wall clock, or restate the bands for a confined case and say so. Both are choices with a cost, which is why this is queued rather than silently applied.

Note the tension: widening the domain makes the M8 minute harder at the same time as it makes the M8 bands reachable.
dropped_reason: Fixed in T110 (session 22): D-075 gives flow/autoconfig.py Rung 3's own domain (SPAN_D 24, UPSTREAM_D 8). The product path now reads Cd 1.4030 where Rung 3 itself prints 1.4031, and Rung E passes with the published bands unwidened.
title: [autoconfig] the product path's domain gives Cd 1.60 / St 0.184 at Re 100, outside Rung 3's bands

body: Case.explain() renders the suggestions carried on the Unrepresentable (autoconfig's), then prints 'Case.nearest() applies the first of these'. Case.nearest() actually takes the top of Case.suggestions, which is flow.diagnose.suggest()'s ranked list -- and D-063 has diagnose prepend a 'fluid' option that autoconfig never creates. Measured on air / 5 m/s / 10 cm (Re 32982): explain() prints 1. speed -> 0.018192 m/s, 2. size -> 0.00036384 m; nearest() runs fluid -> honey. The sentence at flow/case.py:548 is therefore false whenever a fluid substitution is available. The two lists agree on D-038's own air/20/1.5 case (Re 2e6, no fluid is thick enough), which is why T108's tests did not catch it. Found in T109 while wiring the CLI's refusal output; flow/cli.py prints case.suggestions (the executed list) rather than repeating the claim, so the CLI is honest, but explain() itself still is not. Fix is one of: have explain() render case.suggestions, or drop the 'first of these' sentence.
dropped_reason: Closed by T204 / D-093. The divergence was measured on D-038's own case (explain showed speed,size; nearest ran fluid->honey) and that case is no longer refused at all: the closure engages and it runs, banded. Every refusal that remains is a relaxation refusal about an inviscid fluid, whose fix is a fluid from both code paths, and flow.diagnose._present now dedupes by (change, value) -- so the two lists agree on every reachable refusal. tests/test_cli.py::test_the_suggestions_the_cli_prints_are_the_ones_nearest_would_run now iterates validate.refusals.CASES and asserts the agreement rather than pinning the divergence.
title: [case] explain()'s 'What would work' list is not the list nearest() acts on

body: The cost check compares bare vs watched steps/s with alternating rounds (D-035) and fails at >=2%. Measured readings across sessions: D-061's four at +1.10 / +0.98 / -1.09 / -2.10%, session 19 at 0.01%, session 20 at -0.53%, and session 21 at +2.57% (FAIL) then 0.57% (PASS) on a re-run twenty minutes later with nothing else on the machine. Range -2.10% to +2.57% against a +/-2% gate, so the check fails intermittently on measurement noise rather than on a change in Monitor. The failing run was the third of three rungs chained in one shell (R4 -> A -> D); its BARE figure was the fastest of the pair at 253.7 steps/s, so the machine was not slow, the ratio was noisy. D-061 already reads the honest conclusion -- 'below the noise floor, not free'. Options: more alternating rounds before taking the best, a limit set from the measured spread rather than from a round number, or reporting the cost without gating on it. Not a blocker: the rung passes on an idle machine and all three detections are unchanged at 1525/1650, 75/325, 50/59275.

Monitor's own arithmetic is 0.14% of a timestep, measured directly, so the old spread was the machine.
title: [validate] Rung D's Monitor cost check has a spread wider than its own 2% limit

body:
flow/autoconfig.py sets PLAYBACK_SPEED = 1.0 as a module constant and python -m flow exposes no flag for it, so steps_per_frame is always sized for real-time playback. That is right for the 2 cm / water cases the phase was tuned on and useless for a physically small, fast case.

Repro:
  myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m flow --shape examples/shapes/test_shape.png --fluid air --speed '5 m/s' --size '0.36 mm' --explain --backend warp

Prints a valid, runnable plan -- Re 118.7, tau 0.5505 (clears the 0.54 bluff-body floor, D-029), 960x838, 64000 steps -- and then:
  estimated wall clock 73.0 s (1 frames at 60 fps)

The whole flow is 5.76 ms of physical time, so real-time playback keeps one frame. --live has the same problem: steps_per_frame is 185185 against 64000 total steps, so the window would paint once. The numbers (Cd/Cl/St) are unaffected and correct; only the picture is lost, which matters because the picture is the product's stated output.

lbm.runner already has the knob -- '--speed' (playback rate: 1.0 real time, 10.0 ten times faster), lbm/runner.py:1492 -- so this is a flow/ surfacing gap, not a missing capability. Note the name collides with flow's --speed (free-stream velocity), so flow/ would need a different spelling: --playback, or frames-per-run.

Constraint 13 is the thing to think about: playback rate is not a lattice quantity, it is a display quantity, so exposing it does not breach 'no lattice quantity in any public flow/ signature'. Constraint 7 says steps_per_frame is computed from target playback speed and never hardcoded -- it is computed here, but from a hardcoded target, which is arguably the same defect one level up.

Workaround in the tree: scripts/slowmo.py overrides Plan.steps_per_frame via dataclasses.replace after planning, sizing it from the steps the run will actually take. Verified end to end on warp: 30 frames written to a .gif, stable=True. It reaches into case.plan and case._steps(), both of which a product-level flag would make unnecessary.
title: [cli] no playback-speed knob: any sub-millimetre case renders a 1-frame video

body:
Constraint 14: 'Every refusal names a fix, and the fix is machine-checked.' The live divergence probe's message names two: 'Slow the flow down, or raise quality so the same flow is resolved more finely.' For a body with sharp rear corners, MEASURED, neither one does.

Repro (test3.png is a left-pointing wedge with a flat rear face, 40 cells across):
  myenv/Scripts/python.exe -m flow --shape examples/shapes/test3.png --fluid air --speed '3 m/s' --size '0.40 mm' --backend warp --no-live --quiet
  -> Diverging: caught at step 75

The case is not marginal on the published guardrails: Re 79.16, tau 0.5758, which explain() itself calls 'comfortable'. Peak |u| measured in fluid cells only (Monitor already zeroes solid) at the spike location row 458 col 362 -- two cells outside the body's top-right corner, bbox rows 461-500 cols 320-364. So it is the sharp corner of the flat base, not the leading tip.

Both suggested fixes measured, peak |u| over 400 steps, ceiling 0.1:
  3 m/s   balanced  tau 0.5758  peak 0.1344  OVER
  3 m/s   accurate  tau 0.5948  peak 0.1377  OVER
  1.5 m/s balanced  tau 0.6516  peak 0.1200  OVER
  1 m/s   balanced  tau 0.7274  peak 0.1122  OVER
  1 m/s   accurate  tau 0.7843  peak 0.1139  OVER

Slowing by 3x and raising quality both fail because u_lattice is fixed at 0.05 regardless of physical speed (D-032). The corner speedup is geometric -- peak/u_free is about 2.7 for this shape -- so it does not scale with the speed the user types, and tau only damps it slightly.

The lever that does work is u_lattice itself, which flow/ deliberately does not expose (constraint 13):
  u_lattice 0.050  tau 0.5758  peak 0.1344  OVER
  u_lattice 0.040  tau 0.5606  peak 0.1109  OVER
  u_lattice 0.030  tau 0.5455  peak 0.0862  OK
  u_lattice 0.025  tau 0.5379  BELOW 0.54 FLOOR
At 0.03 the full 300-frame run completes and the wake is a clean vortex street.

Root cause candidate: BLUFF_BODY_SPEEDUP is 1.8 (flow/autoconfig.py, cited in explain() as '1.8x it (0.0900) stays under the 0.1 ceiling'). A sharp-cornered body needs about 2.7. The constant is a single number for every geometry, and prepare.py already measures the shape -- corner sharpness is measurable at plan time, so the planner could pick u_lattice from the geometry instead of assuming, and would then either succeed or refuse BEFORE running rather than diverging at step 75.

Note the window between 0.030 (works) and 0.025 (below the tau floor) is narrow, so a geometry-aware u_lattice would also need the quality knob to widen it: tau scales with cells across.

Workaround in the tree: scripts/windtunnel.py --u-lattice, which recomputes tau, run length and vorticity_limit together and re-checks the 0.54 floor.
title: [diagnose] Diverging names two fixes; neither works for a sharp-cornered body (constraint 14)

body:
lbm.render.render() writes solver y=0 into image row 0, and row 0 displays at the TOP of an image, so physical 'up' is drawn at the bottom. LiveSink corrects for this -- 'if self.flip_y: frame = frame[::-1]', lbm/render.py:340, flip_y defaulting True with the docstring 'draw row 0 at the bottom. The solver's y increases...'. RecordSink.push (lbm/record.py:309) and HeadlessSink.push (:423) pass the frame straight to the writer with no flip.

Consequence: the live window and the saved video of the SAME run are vertical mirror images, and the file is the wrong one.

Verified orientation directly:
  ny, nx = 8, 4; f = zeros; f[ny//2:, :] = 1.0   # +1 at LARGE y, i.e. physically up
  img = render(f, 1.0)
  img[0, 0]  -> [221 221 221]   (top row of the image = the ZERO half)
  img[-1, 0] -> [180   4  38]   (bottom row = the +1 half)
So large y lands at the bottom of the rendered image. COOLWARM high is [180 4 38].

from_png's flip_y does NOT cancel this, which is the tempting wrong conclusion. That flip exists to put the MASK into physical orientation (its docstring: 'mirrors the image vertically on load so a wing loaded from a PNG appears the right way up in the live window'). Having done so, render() then mirrors the whole field on the way out. The two compose, they do not cancel: a PNG of a car with the cabin on top comes back as a video with the cabin on the bottom.

Repro: any asymmetric shape. examples/shapes/car.png (cabin above, wheels below) through scripts/windtunnel.py, or python -m flow with --out set, gives an upside-down car. It went unnoticed on a disc, on a tilted blob and on a left-pointing wedge because none of them are obviously handed about the horizontal axis.

Also affects interpretation, not just aesthetics: the sign of vorticity on screen is inverted relative to omega = d(uy)/dx - d(ux)/dy, so 'red is spinning this way' is backwards in every recorded file, and Cl's sign does not visually match the deflection shown. The NUMBERS are all computed in solver space and are unaffected -- Cd, Cl, St are right.

Fix is one line in each file sink (frame[::-1] before write) or, better, hoist the flip so there is one convention for every sink; the LiveSink flag then becomes redundant rather than special. Worth a test that renders an asymmetric field and asserts the written file's row order, since three sinks currently disagree and nothing catches it.

Workaround for existing files: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf vflip out.mp4. scripts/windtunnel.py and scripts/streamlines.py now flip on the way out of _compose.
title: [record] every saved file is vertically mirrored; LiveSink flips, RecordSink and HeadlessSink do not

body: Rung D's D-035 conditions line printed 'AuthenticAMD at 1882 MHz of 3201 MHz, on battery' during T201's ladder re-run, while Win32_Battery.BatteryStatus read 2 (AC/mains) throughout the session and validate/minute.py printed 'power: mains' for the same machine minutes later. One of the two power probes is wrong. D-035 requires the power state beside every absolute timing figure, so a probe that misreports it makes those figures unquotable. Compare the power detection in validate/refusals.py against the one in validate/minute.py and make them share a single implementation.
title: [validate] refusals.py prints 'on battery' while Win32_Battery reports mains

body:
With the closure on, Sim allocates both smag_out (ny, nx) and smag_work (4, ny, nx) through the backend, unconditionally. The Warp backend (T202) ignores smag_work entirely -- a GPU thread has registers, so there is nothing to stage -- so at 2M cells that is 32 MiB of device memory allocated and never read, against a 391 MiB Sim footprint on a 4 GiB card.

Not a blocker: it is correct, it is bounded, and nothing today runs the closure at 2M cells. The fix is small but crosses the T101 seam, so it is a decision rather than a tidy-up: either an optional backend attribute (wants_smag_work) that Sim consults, or moving the scratch decision into the backend's own allocation. T204 and T208 both touch memory and either is a natural place.

Found while implementing T202 (session 25).
title: [runner] Sim allocates smag_work on backends that never read it
